{"rule":"Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and, in the text field, an original fictional passage of about 250 words that comes immediately AFTER the current text in the same invented story.","text":"At the foot of the stairs stood seven narrow doors. Water streamed through the cracks beneath six of them. The seventh was dry.

The boy held up the lantern. Each door bore a name from the cloth, scratched into the iron at the height of Mara’s eyes. Her mother’s was on the dry door. Mara’s was on the next one, where a thin trickle ran across her boots.

From behind her mother’s door came three knocks.

“She’s alive,” Mara whispered.

The boy did not answer. He pointed to the wall opposite the doors, where a row of seven small wheels turned beneath a sheet of glass. The first six moved steadily. The last shuddered and stopped.

Mara pressed her palm against the glass. A brass tooth lay at the bottom of the case—the one that had broken from the key. Above it, faint letters had been cut into the wall: ONE OPENS. ONE CLOSES.

Her mother knocked again, more urgently this time. Mara lifted the clapper. It was heavy even without the cloth, and when she brought it near the glass, the stalled wheel jerked forward.

The knock became a blow. “Don’t open mine,” her mother said.

Mara stepped back. The boy’s lantern shook in his hand, throwing her shadow across all seven doors. Behind her own, something scratched slowly at the iron.

“What did you put in there?” Mara asked.

Her mother was quiet long enough for the wheel to make a full turn.

“Your name,” she said."}
